In the past 3 months, U.S. immigration enforcement has quietly become a surveillance story as much as an enforcement story, and it's undermining everyone's liberties, citizens and immigrants alike. Here's what’s changed, and the tools & apps to know. 🧵

I spoke with Zain Lakhani of the Women's Refugee Commission about all of this. It's one of the most important conversations I've had this year. Full transcript and audio here: austinkocher.substack.com/p/…

We don't yet know the full scale of postpartum and lactating women being detained in violation of ICE's own policies. WRC has built a pregnancy detention tracker with RelevantResearch and this data is still being collected.

There is no legal right to family reunification under U.S. law and no DHS procedure for facilitating it. More than 400 parents sought reunification through Honduran government channels. The report calls for building that system from scratch.

One case from the report: a woman experienced a miscarriage in detention, received no medical oversight for ten days, was deported in an acute medical crisis, and was only saved because reception workers in Honduras rushed her to an emergency room.

ICE's own Detained Parents Directive requires agents to ask every arrestee if they're a parent, to ensure children are safe, and to give parents a choice about whether children accompany them. The report documents routine violations of all three requirements.
Under Biden, 264 mothers were detained and 30% were deported. Under Trump, that's jumped to 800 mothers detained and 60% deported.

What the data doesn't yet tell us: how often courts are actually enforcing these orders versus issuing them and moving on. Contempt threats are meaningful but only if they're followed through.

I saw a similar spike in habeas cases at the start of COVID-19, when ICE detention centers became dangerous infection sites. The mechanism is the same: a surge in enforcement without legal safeguards forces people into court. This spike is larger.

In the Minnesota case, Judge Patrick Schiltz took the U.S. Attorney to task for what he described as an embarrassing response to court concerns. When judges appointed by Republican presidents threaten contempt, that tells you something.

Habeas corpus is the legal mechanism that lets people challenge whether their detention is lawful. It's in Article 1 of the Constitution. The administration has openly discussed suspending it and may not need to if agencies can simply ignore court orders.
